sentences.text: Good evening.
You keep replaying that argument;
tonight, pray with gratitude and entrust the hurt to God.

the spilled cup, the difficult news, the sentence you wish you had answered differently.

In every thing give thanks:
for this is the will of God in Christ Jesus concerning you.
Father, I come with a day that has several stories inside it.
Some moments gave me pleasure;
others left me tired or uncertain.
I want to offer truthful thanks.
Keep me from decorating pain with cheerful words simply because I think I should.
Help me recognize mercy wherever it really appeared.
I bring this whole day before you, trusting that honesty belongs within worship.

Perhaps you found a seat when you needed one, or someone waited while you gathered your things.
Perhaps you had a few minutes outside.
Choose something that really happened to you.
As you recall that detail, you can acknowledge the good it carried.
Let your thanks have the shape of an actual moment, with a place, a person, or a simple object.
Lord, I remember the beginning of this day.
I thank you for whatever helped me enter it:
a familiar voice, a working light, clothing I could put on, or a little food before leaving.
I often hurry past these familiar things.
Tonight I receive them with attention.
Where the morning was difficult, help me remember any kindness that met me there.
I offer thanks for the support I actually had, however modest it may have seemed.
O give thanks unto the LORD;
for he is good:
for his mercy endureth for ever.
You may have received help through someone whose name you know well, or through a person you will never meet again.
You can remember the specific action:
they explained the form, held the elevator, listened carefully, or made space for you.
If no such encounter comes to mind, you can notice another kind of mercy.
You are learning to recognize what was given without comparing your day with another’s.

I remember those whose labor brought them near:
those who grew, carried, stocked, prepared, or shared them.
Let my gratitude reach beyond the meal to the hands behind it.
If I ate alone, receive my thanks from that quiet table.
If I had company, help me cherish the welcome we offered each other, even when our conversation was ordinary and brief.
Father, I give thanks for the places where I could pause today.
Perhaps it was a kitchen chair, a covered doorway, a bench, or a borrowed corner where I could collect myself.
I remember the relief of that brief pause.
Thank you for any shelter and welcome I received.
Make me attentive to those who lack a safe place tonight, and show me a practical way to support their dignity when I am able to help.
You may hear these examples and feel the ache of something you lacked.

You are allowed to bring need into this conversation without apologizing for the space it takes.

Help me recognize trustworthy assistance.

Teach me to receive generosity with dignity and to offer it responsibly when I have enough to share.

great is thy faithfulness.

You can also say that something hurt.

I will not pretend that cruelty was kindness or that disappointment felt easy.

Give me courage to seek safety where it is needed and counsel where I feel unsure.
